group: jsonNodeReader is not null – edge cases

cases.description: Even when a custom JsonNodeReader is present, a null InputStream should cause the underlying reader to throw IllegalArgumentException, which must be propagated.

input.value: InputStream containing malformed YAML: name: John: Doe

cases.description: If JsonNodeReader attempts to parse malformed YAML, it will throw an IOException; the method must propagate it.
When jsonNodeReader is present but inputFormat is null, the JsonNodeReader implementation is expected to reject the null and throw NPE, which should be propagated.
If an unsupported InputFormat enum constant is passed to a non‑null JsonNodeReader, it should raise an exception that the method propagates.
When JsonNodeReader.readTree returns null (e.g., custom implementation decides the content is empty), the method should simply return null without throwing.
If JsonNodeReader.readTree throws an unchecked exception (e.g., RuntimeException), the method must not catch it and should let it propagate.

When jsonNodeReader is null, the method obtains the ObjectMapper for JSON. The mocked ObjectMapper.readTree throws an unchecked IllegalStateException. The method must not catch it and should let the exception propagate.

When jsonNodeReader is null, getObjectMapper(inputFormat) itself throws a NullPointerException (simulating an internal factory failure). The method should propagate this unchecked exception unchanged.
